takeaways: Sovanta's sharpening AI-agent-within-SAP positioning creates a competitive differentiation gap in DACH — SMT should accelerate messaging around its own SAP-Qualtrics integration capabilities for banking and retail clients who need operational-experience data convergence, especially targeting DACH financial services prospects where Sovanta is actively selling.

Higher Oak's continued multi-week content silence represents a potential opportunity to capture UK/EU Qualtrics Platinum Partner mindshare — SMT sales should proactively reach out to Higher Oak's known enterprise clients in UK banking and retail who may be seeking more active partner support and thought leadership.

Acceleration Strategy's sustained post-X4 content dominance in North America, particularly around Qualtrics AI agents, signals that SMT needs a comparable or differentiated content strategy for the US/Canada market — consider co-marketing with Qualtrics on banking-specific AI agent use cases to compete for North American Qualtrics enterprise deals.

The Iberoamerican market (Lukkap + Izo) shows stable but non-AI-forward positioning — SMT can differentiate in Spanish-speaking markets by leading with AI-powered CX and GenAI-specific banking/retail use cases that neither competitor is currently emphasizing, creating a technology-forward positioning gap SMT can exploit.

Globant's absorption of CX messaging into broader AI engineering narratives creates an opportunity with enterprise buyers who want dedicated, specialized CX consulting rather than CX as a sub-service of large-scale IT transformation — SMT should position its focused CX expertise and banking/retail vertical depth as a counter-narrative to Globant's generalist approach in competitive deals.
